title: Blue Owl's BDC Already Cut Its Base Dividend to $0.31. Here's What to Watch as the Rest Report.
author: Reuben Gregg Brewer
description: Blue Owl Capital cut its base dividend from $0.37 to $0.31 per quarter due to declining interest rates on its loan portfolio, which fell from 11.1% to 10%. The dividend cut reflects reduced earnings power rather than credit quality issues. As other BDCs report results, investors should monitor peers like Main Street Capital, Ares Capital, and FS KKR Capital for similar pressures from the changing interest rate environment and portfolio valuations.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Cut base dividend from $0.37 to $0.31 due to declining loan interest rates (11.1% to 10%) and falling NAV per share ($15.14 to $14.41), indicating reduced earnings power and portfolio value deterioration.

While loan rates declined (11.4% to 10.3%), NAV per share increased ($32.03 to $33.46) and non-accrual loans improved. Unlikely to cut dividend with base of $0.795 per share, but faces same interest rate headwinds as peers.
Maintained dividend despite declining loan rates (10.9% to 10.3%), with NII covering the $0.48 dividend. However, NAV declined and non-accrual loans rose to 2.4%, warranting close monitoring.

Already cut dividend from $0.70 to $0.48 per share with base reduced to $0.42. Loan rates fell sharply (11% to 9.9%), NII dropped significantly, NAV fell materially ($23.37 to $18.83), and non-accrual loans surged to 4.2%, indicating serious deterioration.
